chart.title: How paper is recycled
steps: Used paper is collected from homes and offices
Paper is sorted by type and grade at a recycling centre
Paper is mixed with water and chemicals in a pulper to make pulp
Pulp is screened and cleaned to remove plastic and staples
Ink is removed (de-inking); pulp is bleached if necessary
Pulp is pressed and rolled into thin sheets
Sheets are dried by heated rollers
Paper is wound onto large reels and sent to manufacturers

model:
The diagram illustrates the stages involved in recycling used paper so that it can be made into new paper products.
Overall, the process consists of eight steps, beginning with the collection of waste paper and ending with the delivery of new rolls of paper to manufacturers. It can be divided into two main phases: the preparation of pulp and the production of new sheets.
First, used paper is collected from households and offices and taken to a recycling centre, where it is sorted according to its type and quality. It is then placed in a large machine called a pulper and mixed with water and chemicals, which break it down into pulp. Once this has been done, the pulp is screened and cleaned so that unwanted materials such as plastic and staples are removed. After that, the ink is taken out in a de-inking stage, and the pulp may also be bleached if white paper is required.
In the second phase, the clean pulp is pressed and rolled into thin sheets, which are then dried by heated rollers. Finally, the finished paper is wound onto large reels and transported to manufacturers to be made into new products.
modelNotes: Edilgen yapı tutarlı: is collected, is sorted, are removed, is pressed.
